The [Nasdaq Composite](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.IXIC/) was higher on Thursday as the latest earnings reports from [Nvidia](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVDA/) and other well-known technology companies boosted sentiment.

The tech-heavy index rose 1.57% to 26,541.35, while the [S&P 500](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.SPX/) advanced 0.72% end at 7,730.99. The [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.DJI/) climbed 105.56 points, or 0.2%, and closed at 53,569.44.

It was the best day since Aug. 4 for the tech sector, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite.

Nvidia shares jumped 8.7% after it [beat analyst expectations](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/26/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q2-2027-live-updates.html) and forecast strong revenue growth. Notably, the chipmaker is projected to see revenue growth [hit 70%](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/26/nvidia-70percent-growth-forecast-puts-it-on-track-to-be-tech-no-2-company.html) in fiscal 2028, far higher than the 44% that analysts surveyed by LSEG expected. Its revenue for the fiscal second quarter more than doubled.

Shares linked to the semiconductor industry rallied, with [Broadcom](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AVGO/) adding 4.5%, and [SK Hynix](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/SKHY/) and [Intel](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/INTC/) up 2% and 4%, respectively. The [VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH)](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/SMH/) rose 3%.

“There’s been a lot of talk lately about the circular financing for all these hyperscalers and whether revenues will be able to actually cover the huge costs that they’re incurring. Maybe this holds off that discussion for a little while,” said Melissa Brown, global head of investment decision research at SimCorp. Other names in the AI trade are “just riding \[Nvidia’s\] coattails,” she added.

Outside of Nvidia and its fellow chip stocks, [Salesforce](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/CRM/) rallied more than 22% after revenue came in [ahead of Wall Street’s forecast](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/26/salesforce-crm-q2-earnings-report-2027.html) for the second quarter. Software stocks such as [Adobe](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/ADBE/) and [Autodesk](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/ADSK/) climbed 5.7% and 6.2%, respectively.

Within cybersecurity, [Okta](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/OKTA/) soared more than 28% and [CrowdStrike](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/CRWD/) gained 20.5% after [surpassing analyst expectations](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/27/okta-skyrockets-20percent-and-crowdstrike-surges-15percent-leading-cyber-rally.html) and raising their outlooks as the companies see booming demand due to agentic AI. Other cyber stocks such as [Palo Alto Networks](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/PANW/) rose alongside them. That stock in particular popped almost 13%.

Brown noted that because there’s such a divergence between stocks related to the artificial intelligence trade and those in other areas of the market, there’s a low correlation across stocks that’s impacting risk.

“The volatility is high, but the correlation is low, and so that’s keeping overall volatility low,” she said. “Our concern is that that kind of lulls investors into a false sense of security.”

Traders are readying for the Federal Reserve’s annual symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, where Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is [slated to deliver a keynote speech](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/26/fed-survey-warsh-economy-view.html) Friday.

## J.M. Smucker says Uncrustables helped drive expectation-smashing revenue

A box of J.M. Smucker Co. Smucker’s Uncrustables brand peanut butter and grape jelly sandwiches is arranged for a photograph in Tiskilwa, Illinois.

Daniel Acker \| Bloomberg \| Getty Images

[J.M. Smucker](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/SJM/) blew past Wall Street’s revenue expectations for the first fiscal quarter, thanks in part to strength in its Uncrustables brand.

The food producer posted $2.22 billion in revenue for the three-month period, exceeding the expectation of every analyst polled by FactSet. J.M. Smucker said it now expects full-year revenue to shrink less than previously forecast.

CEO Mark Smucker said [in prepared remarks](https://s203.q4cdn.com/703080298/files/doc_financials/2027/q1/The-J-M-Smucker-Co-FY27-Q1-Earnings-Prepared-Remarks.pdf) that the Uncrustable brand saw 12% net sales growth.

Uncrustables is driving momentum in the broader frozen handheld and spreads category, CFO Tucker Marshall said on the company’s Wednesday earnings call. The Ohio-based company is spending some of its tariff refund on pre-production expenses and marketing tied to the brand, Marshall said.

“As you think about Uncrustables, that continues to be a great story,” Marshall said.

J.M. Smucker shares have jumped nearly 8% this week, which would mark its seventh consecutive winning week. The stock has surged 38% in 2026, on track for its first positive year in four.

_— Alex Harring_

## GPU supply constraints will boost DigitalOcean, Truist says

[DigitalOcean](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/DOCN/) is using a constrained GPU market to fortify its business for the long-term, according to Truist Securities.

The bank initiated coverage on the cloud infrastructure provider with a buy rating and a $175 price target. That implies a 52% gain from Wednesday’s close. In a Thursday note, analyst Miller Jump wrote that the company is making strategic moves amid an imbalanced supply and demand environment.

“Management has indicated that the supply demand imbalance is enabling them to handpick the customers that are most aligned with their long-term aspirations as a business,” Jump wrote. “We expect this to translate to large customers that are taking value-added software offerings like DOCN’s managed inference which could make them both stickier and higher-margin.”

Jump added that DigitalOcean doesn’t face the same financing risks as other companies in the GPU buildout, stating that the company isn’t looking to compete with hyperscalers but rather extend its “core value proposition.” Shares were higher by more than 5% in afternoon trading.

## Citi upgrades Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile to buy

Citi analyst Alan Trebitsch on Wednesday upgraded shares of Chilean chemical company [Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/SQM/) to buy, from neutral/high risk, saying the attractively valued stock should get a boost from a recovering lithium market.

“We expect lithium prices to strengthen through YE26, supported by battery supply chain restocking and resilient EV and BESS demand,” Trebitsch wrote. “Citi’s commodities team expects the market to stay in deficit in 2026 before returning to balance in 2027 as suspended capacity restarts and new supply enters the market.”

However, the analyst revised his price target slightly lower to $95, from $97 previously. The new price target still implies more than 20% upside from where the stock closed Wednesday, at $78.28. Shares were last up by 2%.

## Lower oil prices dampens chances for a September rate hike by the Fed, UBS says

Pumpjacks operating in the Permian Basin near Tubb, Texas, US, on Sunday, Aug. 16, 2026.

Kaylee Greenlee \| Bloomberg \| Getty Images

[U.S. oil prices](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/@CL.1/) remain above $80 per barrel, but their decline from late-July highs of above $90 makes the chances of an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve at its September meeting unlikely, according to UBS.

The bank’s chief investment officer for the Americas and global head of equities Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi wrote in a Thursday note that the [bond sell-off](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/18/bond-yields-government-us10y-treasury-note-iran.html) has also been eased by the recent decline in oil prices. However, she added that high yields will likely remain so long as Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh continues to be cautious about giving long-term forecasts.

“The Fed has placed less emphasis on forward guidance, while markets are also considering the implications of a smaller balance sheet over time,” she wrote. “This increases uncertainty around the central bank’s reaction function and raises the compensation investors demand for holding long-duration assets.”

Warsh is set to deliver a keynote speech at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium on Friday. CME’s FedWatch tool as of Thursday morning places nearly two-in-three odds the central bank keeps rates steady at its September meeting.

— _Davis Giangiulio_

## ‘Now is the time to act’ on raising interest rates, Fed’s Hammack says

Beth Hammack, President and CEO of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, speaking with CNBC from Jackson Hole on Aug. 27, 2026.

David A. Grogan \| CNBC

Cleveland Federal Reserve President Beth Hammack on Thursday repeated her call for higher interest rates, saying recent inflation data show the central bank is still too far from its goal.

A report released Wednesday showed inflation running around 3% on an annualized basis, the central bank policymaker said. Even though the monthly rates of price increases have slowed over the past few months, Hammack said the Fed should tighten monetary policy.

“I don’t want to prejudge anything. But I believe now is the time to act,” she said in a live CNBC interview from the Fed’s annual symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyo. “I believe that we’ve been in an inflationary situation for more than five years. It’s been running well above our target. I don’t see any restriction in policy when I look at financial conditions and when I talk to market participants.”

The remarks are in line with others Hammack has made recently. [Read more](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/27/feds-hammack-says-now-is-the-time-to-act-on-raising-interest-rates.html).

_— Jeff Cox_

## Inflation ‘stubborn’ and ‘sticky,’ but policy rate not restrictive, Kansas City Fed’s Schmid says

Jeff Schmid, Kansas City Fed President and CEO, speaking with CNBC from Jackson Hole on Aug. 26th, 2026

David A. Grogan \| CNBC

Kansas City Federal Reserve President Jeffrey Schmid said Thursday that inflation is still too high, though he stopped short of calling for an interest rate hike.

Speaking from the central bank’s annual symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyo. that the Kansas City Fed hosts, Schmid said in a CNBC interview that inflation has proven resilient.

“It’s still stubborn and it’s still sticky, and we’re we’ve got to continue to find ways to break through,” he said on “Squawk Box.” “We’re going to have our work cut out for us as we move into the \[Federal Open Market Committee\] cycle.”

## Jobless claims below forecast

Initial jobless claims edged lower last week, keeping in line with a low layoff trend, the Labor Department reported Thursday.

First-time filings for unemployment benefits for the week ended Aug. 22 totaled a seasonally adjusted 203,000, down 4,000 from the prior period and below the Dow Jones consensus for 208,000.

Continuing claims, which run a week behind, fell by 18,000 to 1.78 million.

## Pernod Ricard sales drop amid demand slump and Iran war

Bottles of Jameson Irish whiskey, Havana Club rum, Beefeater gin, Absolut Vodka, and Olmeca tequila, all produced by Pernod Ricard SA.

Bloomberg \| Getty Images

French drinks giant [Pernod Ricard](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/RI-FR/), which makes Absolut vodka, Jameson whiskey and Kahlua, reported a 3.9% year-on-year decline in full-year net sales on Thursday, driven by weak demand in the U.S. and China.

Full-year net sales totaled 9.4 billion euros, slightly short of a consensus estimate compiled by LSEG. A negative currency impact also hit earnings in 2026, the company said.

Pernod Ricard said it now expects organic net sales growth to fall at the lower end of its 3% to 6% guidance range between 2027 and 2029, citing softness in the American market.

The company said performance had picked up in the second half of its fiscal year, but improvements were hampered by the U.S.-Iran war in its fourth quarter.

The conflict in the Middle East is expected to weigh on sales in the first quarter of its new fiscal year, the firm added.

## Oil extends decline as Oman-Iran talks over Hormuz Strait raise hopes of improved supplies

Oil extended declines Thursday as talks between Oman and Iran over reopening the Strait of Hormuz raise hopes for easing supplies.

Futures for international benchmark [Brent crude](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/@LCO.1/) for October delivery declined 0.63% to $87.29 a barrel. U.S. [West Texas Intermediate futures](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/@CL.1/) for October slipped 0.56% at $81.77 per barrel.

Iran and Oman are working on finalizing details of an agreement to control the Strait of Hormuz, according to a senior ​Iranian source, Reuters reported. This follows comments from Iran’s Revolutionary Guards that the two countries had agreed how to share the waterway.

Concerns over the Middle East conflict, however, still persists.

“A perpetual conflict is being fought in the Middle East, now in its sixth month, significantly longer than the promised four to five weeks,” said Tamas Varga, analyst at PVM Oil Associates, adding that “there is no clear pathway to ending it.”

Any agreement between these two parties does not mean that there will be normalization in oil flows through the key chokepoint, ING said in a note.

“We would likely need to see the US lift its blockade on Iranian ports and ease sanctions on Iran before we see any move towards normalization,” ING added.

China’s industrial profits growth in July slowed to its weakest pace this year, expanding 11.2% from a year earlier, as soft demand and a broader slowdown in the economy weighed on manufacturers.

# Software and Chip Stocks Surge in AI-Fueled Earnings Blowout

![Shradha Dinesh hedcut](https://images.wsj.net/im-52683260?width=40&size=1&pixel_ratio=2)

By

[Shradha Dinesh](https://www.wsj.com/news/author/shradha-dinesh)

,

News Associate

Software and semiconductor stocks are high-flying in morning trading on the backs of stellar Salesforce, Crowdstrike and Nvidia earnings Wednesday.

Salesforce is up more than 20%. The software giant said it was deepening its partnership with Anthropic, boosting investor confidence in its ability to integrate AI into its software.

Crowdstrike gained 18% in morning trading. The cybersecurity provider lifted its guidance as AI-security risks are elevating demand.

Okta and Adobe are among the software providers riding the wave, with morning gains of about 26% and 6%, respectively. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software ETF, a proxy for software stocks, is up 6.5%.

Investors had been bearish on software stocks for months, fearing that AI would strong-arm software as a service providers out of business. Markets have backed off the so-called SaaSpocalypse, for now, at least. The S&P Software and Services ETF has recovered all of its losses and is now up year to date.

## Tracking Market Trends

TradingKey - On August 27, Eastern Time, the three major U.S. stock indices closed higher across the board, led by the Nasdaq. Nvidia's strong earnings report and optimistic revenue outlook reignited the AI trade, driving a sharp rebound in tech, software, and select semiconductor stocks. Although the market is still awaiting policy signals from Federal Reserve Chair Warsh at the Jackson Hole symposium, the resilience of AI demand temporarily outweighed concerns over inflation and high interest rates, helping restore risk appetite.

At the close, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.20% to 53,574.35; the S&P 500 Index gained 0.72% to 7,730.99; and the Nasdaq Composite Index advanced 1.57% to 26,541.35.

In terms of sectors and individual stocks, Nvidia ( [NVDA](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/nasdaq-nvda)) surged 8.74% to $227.98, serving as a primary driver of gains in the Nasdaq and S&P 500. The company's latest quarterly results and long-term revenue outlook alleviated market concerns over slowing AI chip demand, while reinforcing investor confidence in the data center capital expenditure cycle. Broadcom ( [AVGO](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/nasdaq-avgo)) rose 4.49%, further lifting sentiment across the semiconductor sector.

Software and cybersecurity stocks also posted strong performance. Salesforce ( [CRM](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/crm)) jumped 22.55%, driven mainly by robust financial results, raised full-year revenue and profit guidance, and its collaboration with Anthropic's Claude model. CrowdStrike ( [CRWD](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/nasdaq-crwd)) rose 20.5% after reporting better-than-expected second-quarter results and raising its full-year revenue outlook, signaling continued growth in AI security demand. The rebound in software stocks also eased market concerns that "AI would disrupt the business models of traditional software companies."

In commodities, crude oil rebounded. Brent crude ( [UKOIL](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/commodities/brent)) closed up 2.04% at $88.46, while WTI crude ( [USOIL](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/commodities/wti)) gained 1.99% to close at $83.53. The rise in oil prices was primarily driven by uncertainty surrounding US-Iran relations. Market reports indicated that the Trump administration has no intention of reinstating the terms of the June ceasefire agreement, making the resumption of diplomatic talks this week more difficult. Meanwhile, although traffic through the Strait of Hormuz showed slight improvement, it remains below recent average levels, meaning energy transit risks have not been fully eliminated.

In precious metals, gold ( [XAUUSD](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/commodities/gold)) rebounded slightly. Spot gold rose 0.16% to $4,601.95. A weaker U.S. dollar provided support for gold prices, but hotter-than-expected U.S. PCE inflation data for July, rebounding oil prices, and elevated Treasury yields capped further upside. Market focus shifted to Warsh's upcoming speech at the Jackson Hole symposium to gauge whether the Federal Reserve will continue to emphasize inflation risks.

In the crypto market, Bitcoin ( [BTCUSD](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/cryptocurrencies/bitcoin)) climbed back above $80,000, trading around $80,400. The rally in tech stocks and improved risk sentiment supported Bitcoin, though the U.S. dollar, Treasury yields, and Fed policy expectations remain key variables for short-term volatility.

## Market News

**Nvidia pauses revenue-sharing arrangements with AI cloud companies.** Market reports indicate that Nvidia has paused revenue-sharing arrangements with certain AI cloud service providers. The model originally allowed cloud providers to acquire GPUs at lower upfront costs and share subsequent cloud compute revenues with Nvidia. This adjustment signals that Nvidia is reevaluating the business models, financial pressures, and collection risks of its AI cloud customers.

**Anthropic discussed acquiring MatX for about $7 billion.** Sources said Anthropic discussed acquiring AI chip startup MatX in a deal valued at around $7 billion to accelerate its in-house AI hardware layout and support its rapidly growing model training and inference needs. However, Anthropic ultimately abandoned the acquisition plan and has not yet decided to pursue a similar transaction.

**Kioxia and SanDisk plan to invest over $31 billion in Japan.** Kioxia and SanDisk ( [SNDK](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/nasdaq-sndk)) announced plans to invest more than $31 billion in Japan by 2032 to advance memory chip technology and expand production capacity. Among these efforts, Kioxia plans to build a new memory chip production facility at its Kitakami plant in Iwate Prefecture, Japan. As demand for AI servers, enterprise SSDs, and high-performance storage continues to grow, memory chips are becoming a critical link in the AI infrastructure cycle.

**U.S. initial jobless claims fall, showing ongoing labor market resilience.** According to U.S. Department of Labor data, initial jobless claims fell to 203,000 for the week ending August 22, below market expectations. Employment data indicates that while hiring has slowed, layoffs remain low. This data provides room for the Federal Reserve to remain focused on inflation and keeps the market highly sensitive to whether Warsh will deliver hawkish signals at the Jackson Hole symposium.

**Oil price rebound brings inflation risks back into focus.** Crude oil markets repriced geopolitical risk premiums after the Trump administration refused to restore the terms of a previous Iranian ceasefire agreement. Both Brent and WTI crude rebounded, indicating that the market remains concerned about uncertainties surrounding transit through the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian supply, and Middle East shipping security. If oil prices rise again, it could weaken previous market optimism about cooling inflation following the PCE data and continue to impact the Federal Reserve's policy path.
